python3 scripts/goal_guard.py --arm docs/planning/api-1.0-campaign-goal.json
⚠ WHY THIS REPLACED A SLICE-SCOPED GOAL, and it is the whole point of the file.
The slice-A goal was armed at 03:45Z with a 24h deadline and RELEASED ITSELF AT
05:55Z -- two hours in -- with `_cleared_because: all checks passed`. It did
exactly what it was told. It was told the wrong thing: its checks described ONE
SLICE, so finishing that slice satisfied it and the run ended twenty-two hours
early with the campaign barely started.
That is the same failure as the 2026-07-25 incident this guard was BUILT for --
a 24h run ending at 84 minutes -- arriving through the front door instead of
the back. The lesson recorded then was 'never self-impose a budget'. The lesson
now is sharper: A GOAL SCOPED TO A DELIVERABLE IS A BUDGET WEARING A CHECKLIST.
The scope of the goal has to be the scope of the WORK.
So the checks below are api-growth-method.md §4's TERMINAL CONDITION verbatim:
the allowlist ratchet at zero, a blind agent run that opens no engine file, and
every consumer-matrix category proven. None can be satisfied by finishing a
slice. All three are far away, and that is correct -- Jon: 'this will take more
than 24 hours, so there's no point in a stop criteria because you should not
stop'.
⚠ THE ESCAPE HATCHES ARE STILL LIVE, deliberately. A guard that can wedge a
session is worse than no guard, and this one has had that bug twice.
`max_stalled_blocks: 30` releases if thirty blocks pass with NO NEW COMMIT --
so thrashing without landing work still ends the run, which is the behaviour
that should survive. The deadline and `max_run_hours` are backstops that depend
on nothing but the clock.
## The method this goal is enforcing
§1: 'Each slice closes the leak that the previous slice measured as most
expensive, and is not allowed to end until it has produced the measurements
that select the next one.' Base case slice A (closed). Step is §3. Terminal
condition is §4, below.
Every slice: introduce one authority, migrate all production consumers, delete
the displaced authority, guard the absence. All four. A slice that ends with
two paths alive did not land.
Every slice ends by re-running §2's five evidence sources and DERIVING the
next one. A slice that closes a leak and collects no evidence has broken the
induction -- there is nothing to select from next, and slice N+2 gets chosen
by taste.
## Scar tissue, every line of it paid for
* $HOME/.cargo/bin/cargo everywhere -- the hook PATH has no cargo, and a
'command not found' check can NEVER pass, wedging the run it guards.
* Never end a pipeline with `grep -q` under pipefail (SIGPIPE -> exit 141).
* `cargo test` with a filter matching ZERO tests EXITS 0. Assert a POSITIVE
pass count or an unwritten test passes before it exists.
* NEVER grep for the absence of an identifier -- three checks went red on the
prose explaining the removal. Absences go through
check_absence_contracts.py, which strips comments, and the check names the
CONTRACT ID rather than the symbol.
* A RATCHET NEEDS TWO INVARIANTS. `named ⊆ allowed ∪ baseline` is the obvious
half; without `baseline ⊆ named` the baseline is a BUDGET -- retire a member,
leave it listed, and the freed slot fills silently while the count holds.
* A VERDICT COLUMN THAT RESTATES ITS INPUT REPORTS NOTHING. Slice A's §2d
classifier computed `became_deletable = in_scope`, so the most valuable
signal the method produces was empty BY CONSTRUCTION while reporting 2/2.
* AN OVERCLAIMED GUARANTEE IS WORSE THAN AN ABSENT ONE -- it tells a consumer
to stop looking. The blind run caught `ambition::app` claiming rule 7 was
enforced when only a string was checked. Both overclaims were written by
this campaign.
* MEASURE THE PREDICTION BEFORE THE WORK. A number matching a RECORDED
prediction confirms the model; one matching a remembered guess teaches
nothing.
## Deliberately NOT terminal conditions
The bevy_ggrs patch table (Jon deferred it 2026-07-30 pending an upstream
crates.io release) and any `ambition_actors` decomposition (§4 authorises it
only when a leak or a sentinel consumer's footprint demands it, and then only
the boundary that leak NAMES).

⚠ ADDED 2026-07-30 after a check reported FAILED with an EMPTY detail. The guard handles timeouts explicitly, so an empty detail means the command produced no output at all — which these checks did BY DESIGN, piping everything into `grep >/dev/null`. A check that cannot say why it failed is the silent-failure class this campaign exists to hunt, written into the campaign's own instrument. The long-running checks now PRINT the failing lines before exiting nonzero. Still no `grep -q` in any pipeline: it exits on first match, the writer takes SIGPIPE, and pipefail turns the check into a nondeterministic 141.
goal: Run the API 1.0 campaign to its TERMINAL CONDITION by induction: each slice closes the leak the previous slice measured as most expensive, migrates every consumer, DELETES the displaced path, guards the absence, and ends by collecting api-growth-method.md §2's five evidence sources and deriving the next slice from them. Slice A is closed and slice B is derived (the movement-only minimal game). The campaign ends only when all three §4 conditions hold: the allowlist ratchet is at ZERO, a blind agent run completes WITHOUT OPENING AN ENGINE FILE, and EVERY consumer-matrix category has a proof that is a test. This will take many days. There is no deliverable whose completion releases you -- if a slice looks done, that means the next one needs deriving from the evidence you just collected, not that the work is over. Do not stop.

checks.name: §4.1 TERMINAL: the allowlist ratchet is at ZERO — consumers name only the SDK
§4.3 TERMINAL: EVERY consumer-matrix category has a proof, and each proof names a test
checks.cmd: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('docs/planning/engine/slice-evidence/consumer-matrix.json')); u=[c['id'] for c in d['categories'] if not c.get('proven')]; sys.exit('unproven categories: %s'%u) if u else None; n=[c['id'] for c in d['categories'] if not c.get('proof')]; sys.exit('proven with no named proof: %s'%n) if n else None"

checks.name: §4.2 TERMINAL: the latest blind-agent run opened NO engine file
checks.cmd: python3 -c "import json,glob,sys; f=sorted(glob.glob('docs/planning/engine/slice-evidence/blind-agent-runs/*.json')); sys.exit('no blind-agent run recorded') if not f else None; d=json.load(open(f[-1])); opened=d.get('first_engine_file_opened'); surfaces=d.get('engine_api_surfaces_read') or []; sys.exit('latest run opened %r and read %d engine API surfaces'%(opened,len(surfaces))) if (opened or surfaces) else None"

checks.name: INDUCTION: every ratchet holds and every contract is still RED-PROBED
INDUCTION: slice A's consumer has not regressed — Outlander composes through the facade and passes
checks.cmd: out=$($HOME/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path fixtures/external_consumer/Cargo.toml --test composition --test gameplay 2>&1); c=$(echo "$out" | grep -cE "test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed"); if [ "$c" -lt 2 ]; then echo "$out" | grep -E "FAILED|panicked|error\[" | head -15; exit 1; fi

checks.name: the workspace compiles, tests included
checks.cmd: out=$($HOME/.cargo/bin/cargo check --workspace --all-targets --quiet 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then echo "$out" | grep -E "^error" -A 3 | head -20; exit 1; fi

checks.name: the backbone suite is green
checks.cmd: out=$(./run_tests.sh --fast 2>&1); rc=$?; if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || echo "$out" | grep "test result: FAILED" >/dev/null; then echo "$out" | grep -E "^(test |    )[a-z_:]+ \.\.\. FAILED|test result: FAILED|FAILED jobs" | head -20; echo "--- exit $rc ---"; exit 1; fi; echo "$out" | grep -E "test result: ok" >/dev/null
